story.title: feat: add bundle size report to build output

events.body: Adds an optional build.reportSize setting. When enabled, `vite build` prints a table of output files with raw and gzip sizes and flags files that grew compared to the previous build. Off by default.

cannedOutput.headline: vite merges an optional bundle size report for builds
cannedOutput.whatHappened: The vite project merged a change that adds an optional size report to its build command. The change is in the main code but is not part of a published version yet.
cannedOutput.previously: Developers had to use separate tools to see how big each output file was after a build.
cannedOutput.whatChanged: A new build.reportSize setting prints a table of output files with their sizes. It also points out files that grew since the last build. It is off unless you turn it on.
cannedOutput.whyItMatters: Web developers could spot pages getting heavier before their users notice slower loading. People using current versions of vite do not have this yet.
cannedOutput.nextConfirmed: No release date for this change has been announced.
cannedOutput.nextSpeculative: The setting might appear in the next vite version.

glossary.definition: The packed files a build tool creates for a website, ready to send to browsers.
A common way to compress files so they download faster.
Accepted into the main code. It still needs a release before most people can use it.

cannedOutput.analogy: It is like a moving company adding a scale that weighs every box and flags the ones that got heavier since the last move.
cannedOutput.intermediate: Pull request #20811 adds a build.reportSize option. When enabled, vite build prints raw and gzip sizes per output file and flags growth.
cannedOutput.technical: The opt-in build.reportSize setting reports raw and gzip sizes for emitted files and compares them with the previous build to flag growth. Default behavior is unchanged.
